rationale: Coverage: The review addresses all required points: what can be done in simulation (training setup screening, skill pre-training), what requires real data (transfer metric validation, real task verification), how to reduce real-robot training overhead (transfer metric, composable skills), comparison of three evidence types (simulation success, real-trajectory prediction, real-robot verification), and why simulation success or metric correlation cannot replace real-robot verification. It explicitly excludes the predictive maintenance paper as irrelevant. However, the comparison is limited by the abstracts and lacks quantitative details, so not full marks. Factuality: All claims are supported by the provided abstracts. The review correctly distinguishes between correlation evidence (2009.12864v1) and real-robot verification (1809.10253v3), and appropriately labels the conclusion about not replacing real-robot verification as inferential rather than established. No contradictions with abstracts. Citation support: Each major claim is linked to the correct paper ID. The predictive maintenance paper is cited and correctly identified as irrelevant. The review does not overstate support; it notes limitations. Consistency: The review maintains consistent terminology and scope, clearly separates evidence types, and does not contradict itself. The conclusion aligns with earlier sections.
